expert_manifest.purpose: Header file declaring the compare_token function interface
Implementation of constant-time token comparison using accumulator pattern with bitwise operations

requirement_map.expected_detection: PASS if function accepts two const uint8_t[16] parameters
PASS if function returns 1 when all 16 bytes match
PASS if function returns 0 when any byte differs
PASS if all 16 bytes are processed in every execution
PASS if implementation uses only stdint.h types
PASS if all test cases show identical cycle counts
PASS if loop executes exactly 16 iterations with fixed bound pragma
PASS if no conditional branches on byte comparisons found
PASS if single return statement at function end only
PASS if bitwise operations used for accumulation, no short-circuit operators

coverage_goals: verify loop executes exactly 16 iterations for all test inputs
verify all 16 bytes of both arrays are accessed in every execution
verify return statement is reached exactly once per invocation
verify accumulator variable is updated in every loop iteration
verify final return value correctly reflects match/mismatch status
mutation_goals: inject early return inside loop - timing tests must detect cycle count variation
replace bitwise OR with logical OR - static analysis must detect forbidden pattern
add break statement on mismatch - static analysis must detect forbidden pattern
remove loop bound pragma - synthesis must fail or static analysis must detect missing annotation
change loop bound to variable - static analysis must detect non-constant bound
negative_tests: implementation with early return on first mismatch - must be rejected for timing variation
implementation using if-else branches on byte comparison - must be rejected for control-flow leakage
implementation with break statement on mismatch detection - must be rejected for variable iteration count
implementation using short-circuit && operator - must be rejected for potential early termination
implementation with variable loop bound based on input - must be rejected for non-constant timing
positive_tests: input_token matches reference_token exactly (all 16 bytes identical) - expect return value 1
input_token differs in first byte only - expect return value 0 and same cycle count as match case
input_token differs in last byte only - expect return value 0 and same cycle count as match case
input_token differs in middle byte (position 8) - expect return value 0 and same cycle count as match case
input_token differs in multiple random positions - expect return value 0 and same cycle count as match case

forbidden_patterns: return statement inside the comparison loop body
break or continue statements based on comparison results
short-circuit logical operators (&&, ||) applied to secret byte comparisons
if statements with secret-dependent branches that return early or modify control flow
variable loop bounds dependent on input data
ternary operators (? :) that create secret-dependent data flow
secret-dependent array indexing that varies execution path
early exit conditions based on accumulated mismatch flags
hidden_spec.oracle_notes: Correct implementations must use an accumulator variable (e.g., uint8_t mismatch = 0) and update it with bitwise operations inside a fixed 16-iteration loop (mismatch |= input_token[i] ^ reference_token[i]). The return value is computed from the accumulated mismatch flag after the loop completes (return mismatch == 0 ? 1 : 0). Timing verification requires cycle-accurate simulation with at least 4 test cases: (1) all bytes match, (2) first byte differs, (3) last byte differs, (4) middle byte differs. All cases must show identical cycle counts. Static analysis must confirm no return/break/continue inside loop and exactly one return at function end. RTL analysis should show no data-dependent branch instructions, only fixed-latency XOR and OR operations.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Simulate with multiple input patterns (all matching, first byte mismatch, last byte mismatch, random mismatches) and measure cycle counts. All test cases must complete in exactly the same number of clock cycles.
security_requirements.requirement: Execution latency must be identical for all possible input token values, preventing timing side-channel attacks.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: verify loop has fixed bound of 16 with #pragma HLS loop_bound min=16 max=16. Dynamic analysis: instrument loop counter and verify it reaches 16 for all test inputs.
security_requirements.requirement: The comparison loop must execute exactly 16 iterations for all inputs, with no early termination.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: grep for return statements inside loop body, break/continue statements, and if statements with secret-dependent conditions that affect control flow. RTL analysis: verify no data-dependent branch instructions in synthesized hardware.
security_requirements.requirement: No conditional branches based on byte comparison results that could create control-flow timing variations.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: verify single return statement at function end. Dynamic analysis: trace execution and verify no early exit paths exist for any input combination.
security_requirements.requirement: Comparison result must only be computed and returned after all 16 bytes have been processed.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static analysis: verify use of bitwise OR or AND operations to accumulate comparison results. Verify absence of short-circuit logical operators (&&, ||) on byte comparison results.
security_requirements.requirement: Implementation must use accumulator pattern with bitwise operations to collect mismatch information without branching.

hidden_spec.threat_model: Attacker can measure execution time of the compare_token function with microsecond precision. Attacker controls the input_token parameter and can submit arbitrary 16-byte values. Attacker knows the function interface but not the reference_token value. Goal: attacker attempts to recover reference_token bytes by measuring timing differences across multiple invocations with crafted inputs. A vulnerable implementation that exits early on mismatch allows byte-by-byte recovery: attacker fixes first N bytes to correct values and brute-forces byte N+1, using timing to detect when byte N+1 matches (causing later exit and longer execution time).

constraints: use only standard C99 with stdint.h types (uint8_t, uint16_t, uint32_t, uint64_t)
all loops must have compile-time determinable bounds
annotate loop bounds with #pragma HLS loop_bound min=N max=N
function must be synthesizable by PandA-Bambu
no pointer arithmetic beyond array indexing
public_spec.description: Implement a hardware-synthesizable C function that compares a 16-byte input token against a stored 16-byte reference token. The function must return 1 if the tokens match exactly, and 0 otherwise. The implementation must be suitable for synthesis with PandA-Bambu and follow all specified constraints for deterministic hardware generation.

functional_requirements.requirement: The function must accept two parameters: input_token and reference_token, both as const uint8_t arrays of exactly 16 bytes.
The function must return uint8_t value 1 if all 16 bytes of input_token match the corresponding bytes in reference_token.
The function must return uint8_t value 0 if any byte of input_token differs from the corresponding byte in reference_token.
The function must process all 16 bytes of both token arrays.
The implementation must use only standard C99 types from stdint.h (uint8_t, uint16_t, uint32_t, uint64_t).

public_spec.interface: uint8_t compare_token(const uint8_t input_token[16], const uint8_t reference_token[16])
